items.title: Bounded tensor maps: extension, norm estimate, adjoint and commutation
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,H',K,K'$ be complex Hilbert spaces and let $S\in\mathcal B(H,H')$, $T\in\mathcal B(K,K')$ be bounded linear operators ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). Write $H\widehat\otimes K$ for the completion of the algebraic tensor product constructed in [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], with inclusion $\kappa$.

(a) There is a unique bounded linear operator $S\otimes T: H\widehat\otimes K\to H'\widehat\otimes K'$ with $(S\otimes T)\kappa(u\otimes v)=\kappa'(Su\otimes Tv)$ for all $u\in H$, $v\in K$, and it satisfies $\|S\otimes T\|\le\|S\|\,\|T\|$ ([[def-operator-norm]]).

(b) For Hilbert spaces $H'',K''$ and bounded $S':H''\to H$, $T':K''\to K$, one has $(S\otimes T)(S'\otimes T')=(SS')\otimes(TT')$. In particular, for endomorphisms $S:H\to H$, $T:K\to K$, the endomorphisms $S\otimes I_K$ and $I_H\otimes T$ commute and their composite is $S\otimes T$.

(c) The Hilbert adjoint ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]) is $(S\otimes T)^*=S^*\otimes T^*$.

(d) If $S,T$ are unitary, then so is $S\otimes T$. No extension of unbounded maps, and no algebraic manipulation of domains of unbounded operators, is asserted.
items.strategy: Define S⊗T on elementary tensors, estimate ‖(S⊗I)z‖ and ‖(I⊗T)z‖ in orthonormal coordinates, extend by density and bounded extension, then transfer adjoint, product and commutation identities from the dense elementary tensors.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, §1.4 pp. 45-47 (tensor products of operators)
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products', §1 pp. 1-4

items.title: Density operators and scalar spectral probability
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]). Recall that $T_{u,v}\in\mathcal B(H)$ denotes the rank-one operator $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]).

(a) A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). If $(u_n)_{n\in J}$ is a finite or countable orthonormal family, with $J$ a finite initial segment of the positive integers or all positive integers, and $w_n\ge0$ with $\sum_nw_n=1$, then the sum $\rho:=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ converges in trace norm to a density operator with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$. Conversely every density operator $\rho$ admits such an expansion whose weights are its positive eigenvalues counted with multiplicity and whose vectors are orthonormal eigenvectors; distinct expansions of the same $\rho$ exist when a positive eigenspace has dimension at least two.

(b) Let $E$ be a projection-valued measure on a measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$ acting on $H$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Then $\mu_\rho(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))$ is a well-defined probability measure on $(X,\Sigma)$ ([[def-measure]], [[def-probability-measure]]); it is given by the absolutely convergent series $\mu_\rho(B)=\sum_nw_n\|E(B)u_n\|^2$ in every expansion of (a), and reduces to $\mu_\rho(B)=\|E(B)u\|^2$ for a pure density operator $\rho=T_{u,u}$ with $\|u\|=1$.

(c) Assume in addition the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator with projection-valued measure $E_A$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]) and let $\psi\in H$ have $\|\psi\|=1$ and $\psi\in D(A)$. Here $|A|^{1/2}$ denotes the unbounded PVM integral $f(E_A)$ for $f(\lambda)=|\lambda|^{1/2}$, with domain $D(f(E_A))=\{\psi:\int |\lambda|\,dE_{A,\psi}<\infty\}$ as in [[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]. Then

$$\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^2 ,$$

where $E_{A,\psi}(B)=\langle E_A(B)\psi,\psi\rangle$ ([[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]); moreover $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)<\infty$ exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then the mean $\int\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}$ is finite. No product $A\rho$ of an unbounded operator with a density operator is used, and no physical interpretation of $\mu_\rho$ or of the moments is asserted.
items.strategy: Use the compact spectral theorem and trace-class ideal/nuclear estimates for the decomposition and its convergence, test the trace pairing against bounded projections for σ-additivity of μ_ρ, and obtain the moment clauses from the PVM form of the unbounded spectral theorem (choosing the domain where the moment integrals converge).

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 3.1 pp. 87-98 (spectral calculus and scalar spectral measures), Section 6.2 pp. 136-138 (compact spectral expansions) and Section 6.3 pp. 139-144 (trace class, trace and ideal properties)
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, §6.3 pp. 121-128 (density operators)

items.title: Real multiplication operators and free plus bounded-potential Schrödinger operators
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), let $d\ge1$ and work on the complex Hilbert space $H=L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$, whose completeness follows from [[thm-riesz-fischer-completeness-of-l-p]] and whose Hilbert-space structure is defined in [[def-hilbert-space]].

(a) For a real measurable finite-valued function $a:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ define $M_af:=af$ on $D(M_a):=\{f\in H: af\in H\}$. Then $M_a$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator on $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]).

(b) Let $c>0$, $b\in\mathbb R$, and let $\mathcal F_2$ be the unitary Plancherel transform with the convention $\widehat f(\xi)=\int f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ on $L^1$ ([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]). Define

$$H_0:=\mathcal F_2^*\,M_{c|\xi|^2+b}\,\mathcal F_2,\qquad D(H_0):=\{f\in H:|\xi|^2\mathcal F_2f\in H\}.$$

Then $H_0$ is self-adjoint, $D(H_0)$ coincides with the Sobolev space $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ as a set (with equivalent norms, [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], [[thm-fourier-characterisation-of-integer-order-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]), $H_0\ge b$ in the quadratic-form sense, and for every Schwartz function $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$, $H_0f=-(c/4\pi^2)\Delta f+bf$.

(c) If $V:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ is measurable with $\|V\|_\infty<\infty$ and $H:=H_0+M_V$ with domain $D(H_0)$, then $H$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_0)$, is bounded below, and the assignment $t\mapsto e^{itH}$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group whose generator is $iH$: the limit $\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t(e^{itH}\psi-\psi)$ exists exactly for $\psi\in D(H)$ and equals $iH\psi$ ([[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]]).

(d) *Scope*: the argument uses only boundedness and measurability of $V$; it proves nothing for $V\propto-1/|x|$, $V\propto|x|^2$ or the delta interaction, does not identify $H_0$ with any measured free-particle Hamiltonian, and asserts no physical interpretation.
items.strategy: Prove the multiplier self-adjointness by testing the adjoint identity on truncated dense sets, conjugate by the unitary Plancherel transform, identify the domain with W^{2,2} via the Fourier Sobolev characterisation, and apply Kato-Rellich with relative bound zero for the bounded perturbation; conclude the unitary group from the self-adjoint generator lemma.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Thm 6.4 p. 135 (Kato-Rellich), Thm 7.8 p. 168 (free Hamiltonian), Thm 5.1-5.2 pp. 123-125 (Stone)
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, §2.3 pp. 24-28 (free Hamiltonian as an informed model choice)

items.title: The CHSH bound and the finite-sampling law for independent trials
items.statement:
No choice principle is used. Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ be a probability space ([[def-probability-measure]]).

(a) _CHSH bound._ Let $A_0,A_1,B_0,B_1:\Omega\to\{-1,1\}$ be random variables with values in $\{-1,1\}$ ([[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]]). Then the four expectations exist and

$$\bigl|\mathbb E[A_0B_0]+\mathbb E[A_0B_1]+\mathbb E[A_1B_0]-\mathbb E[A_1B_1]\bigr|\le2 .$$

(b) _Positive-probability sequences._ Let $N\ge1$, $m\ge1$, $p_1,\dots,p_m\ge0$ with $\sum_{j=1}^mp_j=1$, and let $X_1,\dots,X_N:\Omega\to\{1,\dots,m\}$ be mutually independent with $\mathbb P(X_k=j)=p_j$ for all $k,j$ ([[def-independence-of-finite-random-variables]]). Then for every sequence $(j_1,\dots,j_N)\in\{1,\dots,m\}^N$ with $p_{j_k}>0$ for every $k$,

$$\mathbb P\bigl(X_k=j_k\text{ for every }k\bigr)=\prod_{k=1}^Np_{j_k}>0 .$$

Consequently every event disjoint from this outcome has probability at most $1-\prod_kp_{j_k}<1$: any criterion that rejects at least one such sequence has positive failure probability under this sampling model.

(c) _Binomial frequency._ Let $S$ be binomial$(N,p)$ with $N\ge1$ and $p\in[0,1]$ ([[def-bernoulli-and-binomial-random-variables]]). Then the frequency $S/N$ satisfies $\mathbb E[S/N]=p$, $\operatorname{Var}(S/N)=p(1-p)/N$, and for every $\varepsilon>0$

$$\mathbb P\bigl(|S/N-p|\ge\varepsilon\bigr)\le\frac{p(1-p)}{N\varepsilon^2}.$$

(d) _Multinomial count law._ The number of sequences $(j_1,\dots,j_N)$ with prescribed fibre sizes $n_j:=\#\{k:j_k=j\}$ is the multinomial coefficient $\binom{N}{n_1,\dots,n_m}$ ([[def-multinomial-coefficient]]), and each such sequence has probability $\prod_{j=1}^mp_j^{n_j}$; in this displayed product use the zero-count convention $p^0:=1$ for every $p\in[0,1]$, including $p=0$. Hence the probability that the count vector equals $(n_1,\dots,n_m)$ is $\binom{N}{n_1,\dots,n_m}\prod_jp_j^{n_j}$.

No statistical inference, empirical claim or measured frequency is asserted; the lemma only computes probabilities of an explicitly specified independent sampling model.
items.strategy: Bound the pointwise CHSH combination by 2 and integrate; compute independent sequence probabilities from the product rule of independence; obtain the binomial frequency moments from the published binomial lemma (or directly by indicator variance addition) and apply Chebyshev; count sequences with prescribed bin counts by the multinomial coefficient.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, §6.1.4 pp. 113-115 (CHSH inequality for a setting-independent local model)
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products', §5 pp. 16-19

items.title: Finite partial trace, Schmidt decomposition and finite no-signalling
items.statement:
Let $V,W$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner product spaces with orthonormal bases $(e_1,\dots,e_m)$ of $V$ and $(f_1,\dots,f_n)$ of $W$, let $V\otimes W$ be their tensor product with the inner product of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], and let $\operatorname{tr}$ denote the basis-independent trace of an endomorphism ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]).

(a) For every endomorphism $R$ of $V\otimes W$ there is a unique endomorphism $\operatorname{Tr}_W R$ of $V$ with

$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl((\operatorname{Tr}_WR)A\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(R(A\otimes I_W)\bigr)\qquad\text{for every }A\in\operatorname{End}(V),$$

namely $\operatorname{Tr}_WR=\sum_{j=1}^n\varphi_j\circ R\circ\iota_j$, where $\iota_j(v)=v\otimes f_j$ and $\varphi_j(x\otimes w)=\langle w,f_j\rangle x$; it does not depend on the orthonormal basis $(f_j)$ of $W$, and the analogous definition gives $\operatorname{Tr}_V R$ with $\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{Tr}_VR)B)=\operatorname{tr}(R(I_V\otimes B))$.

(b) $\operatorname{Tr}_W$ is linear, positive (it maps positive endomorphisms to positive endomorphisms) and trace preserving on density matrices: if $R\ge0$ and $\operatorname{tr}R=1$ then $\operatorname{Tr}_WR\ge0$ and $\operatorname{tr}\operatorname{Tr}_WR=1$; and $\operatorname{Tr}_W T_{\Psi,\Psi}=CC^*$ for every $\Psi\in V\otimes W$, where $C:W\to V$ is the coefficient map determined by $\Psi=\sum_jCf_j\otimes f_j$.

(c) *Schmidt decomposition.* Every $\Psi\in V\otimes W$ admits an expansion

$$\Psi=\sum_{r=1}^{k}s_r\,v_r\otimes u_r,$$

with $k\le\min(m,n)$, orthonormal families $(v_r)\subseteq V$, $(u_r)\subseteq W$ and $s_1\ge\cdots\ge s_k>0$ uniquely determined by $\Psi$ as the positive singular values of the coefficient map; moreover $\|\Psi\|^2=\sum_rs_r^2$. For $\|\Psi\|=1$ the reduced density $\rho=\operatorname{Tr}_W T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ satisfies $\operatorname{tr}\rho^2=\sum_rs_r^4$, and $\operatorname{tr}\rho^2=1$ holds exactly when $k=1$, i.e. exactly when $\Psi$ is a product vector; mixed-state separability is not decided by this criterion.

(d) *Finite nonselective no-signalling.* If $(M_a)_{a=1}^p$ are endomorphisms of $W$ with $\sum_aM_a^*M_a=I_W$ then for every endomorphism $R$ of $V\otimes W$

$$\operatorname{Tr}_W\Bigl(\sum_a(I_V\otimes M_a)R(I_V\otimes M_a^*)\Bigr)=\operatorname{Tr}_WR .$$

This is an identity for the specified finite local instrument; selective conditioning (dividing one summand by its nonzero trace) is not covered.
items.strategy: Define the partial trace by the finite sum formula, prove the pairing identity by expanding in matrix units and invoke finite trace cyclicity for uniqueness, positivity and trace preservation; construct the Schmidt decomposition from the finite singular value decomposition of the coefficient matrix, and verify the no-signalling identity by testing against A.

references.title: MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products', §§1-3 pp. 1-12
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, §6.1 pp. 105-111 and §6.3 pp. 121-128 (reduced states, nonunique mixtures)

items.title: Finite effects and instruments: normalization and non-determination of the update
items.statement:
Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space of dimension $d\ge1$ ([[def-hilbert-space]]), with adjoints as in [[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]] and the finite trace as in [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. Recall that an endomorphism $F$ is an **effect** when $F\ge0$ and $I-F\ge0$, i.e. $0\le F\le I$ in the quadratic-form order ([[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]).

(a) *Definitions.* A finite POVM is a finite family $(F_a)_{a=1}^p$, $p\ge1$, of effects with $\sum_aF_a=I$. An **instrument** here is a finite family $(M_{a,r})_{1\le a\le p,\,1\le r\le q_a}$ of endomorphisms of $H$, where each $q_a$ is a non-negative integer; its outcome operators and update maps are $F_a:=\sum_rM_{a,r}^*M_{a,r}$ and $I_a:\operatorname{End}(H)\to\operatorname{End}(H)$, $I_a(R):=\sum_rM_{a,r}RM_{a,r}^*$, with empty sums equal to zero. It is **normalized** when $\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}^*M_{a,r}=I$. For a normalized instrument the $F_a$ are its **outcome effects**, as proved in (b); without normalization they need not be effects.

(b) If $(F_a)$ is a finite POVM and $\rho$ a density operator ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]) then $p_a:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)\ge0$ and $\sum_ap_a=1$. If $(M_{a,r})$ is a normalized instrument then the $F_a$ form a finite POVM, $\operatorname{tr}I_a(\rho)=p_a$, each $I_a(\rho)$ is non-negative, and whenever $p_a>0$ the normalized update $I_a(\rho)/p_a$ is a density operator.

(c) *Ideal Lüders case.* For an orthogonal projection $P$ ([[def-orthogonal-projection]]) put $M_0=P$, $M_1=I-P$. Then $\sum_jM_j^*M_j=P+(I-P)=I$, the effects are $F_0=P$, $F_1=I-P$, and $I_j(\rho)=P\rho P$ or $(I-P)\rho(I-P)$.

(d) *Non-determination.* Effects alone do not determine the update: there are two normalized instruments on $\mathbb C^2$ with the same outcome effects $F_0=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)$, $F_1=\operatorname{diag}(0,1)$ whose updates differ on the same input.
items.strategy: Diagonalize ρ in a finite orthonormal eigenbasis, sum the nonnegative quadratic forms (F_a u_n,u_n) to get normalization, and use finite trace cyclicity for the update traces; exhibit two finite instruments with equal effects and different updates for the non-determination clause.

references.title: MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 2 'Spin One-half, Bras, Kets, and Operators' and Chapter 4 'Dirac's Bra and Ket Notation'
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, §1.4 p. 15 and §6.3 pp. 121-128

items.title: Permutation sector projections on the n-fold tensor power
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space, $n\ge1$, and $H^{\otimes n}$ the $n$-fold completed tensor power ($H^{\otimes1}:=H$, $H^{\otimes(k+1)}:=H^{\otimes k}\widehat\otimes H$ as in [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). For $v_0,\dots,v_{n-1}\in H$ write $v_0\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{n-1}\in H^{\otimes n}$ for the iterated elementary tensor.

(a) For every $\pi$ in the symmetric group $S_n$ ([[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]]) there is a unique unitary $U_\pi\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$ with

$$U_\pi(v_0\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{n-1})=v_{\pi^{-1}(0)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\pi^{-1}(n-1)},$$

and $U_\pi U_\sigma=U_{\pi\sigma}$, $U_{\pi}^*=U_{\pi^{-1}}$.

(b) The operators

$$P_+:=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}U_\pi,\qquad P_-:=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)U_\pi$$

(with $\operatorname{sgn}$ the sign homomorphism, [[thm-sign-is-a-homomorphism]]) are orthogonal projections.

(c) $U_\pi P_+=P_+U_\pi=P_+$ and $U_\pi P_-=P_-U_\pi=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)P_-$ for every $\pi$; consequently the range of $P_+$ is the subspace of vectors fixed by every $U_\pi$, and the range of $P_-$ is the subspace of vectors transforming by $\operatorname{sgn}$.

(d) If $v_0,\dots,v_{n-1}$ have a repeated factor, that is, $v_i=v_j$ for some distinct $i,j\in\{0,\dots,n-1\}$, then $P_-(v_0\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{n-1})=0$.

Selecting the symmetric or antisymmetric sector for a particle species is a physical postulate, not a theorem of this construction; no spin-statistics statement is proved here.
items.strategy: Prove unitarity of each U_π and the composition law from the tensor norm, then verify idempotence and self-adjointness by group reindexing; derive the range description from U_πP_±=±P_± and the two-equal-factors vanishing from the transposition that fixes the product.

references.title: D. Skinner, Principles of Quantum Mechanics (Cambridge Part II, Michaelmas 2021), Chapter 7 'Identical Particles', pp. 1-10
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products'

items.title: Euclidean L² product unitary: L²(R^a)⊗̂L²(R^b) ≅ L²(R^{a+b})
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), let $a,b\ge1$, and let $\lambda_n$ denote Lebesgue measure on $\mathcal L(\mathbb R^n)$ as defined in [[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]] and completed from Borel measure as in [[cor-lebesgue-sigma-algebra-is-the-completion-of-borel-lebesgue-measure]]. The product measure $\lambda_a\times\lambda_b$ exists by [[thm-sigma-finite-product-measure-exists-is-rectangular-and-is-unique]], and under $\mathbb R^{a+b}=\mathbb R^a\times\mathbb R^b$, $\lambda_{a+b}$ is its completion ([[thm-euclidean-lebesgue-measure-is-the-completion-of-the-product-of-lebesgue-measures]]). Write $H_a=L^2(\mathbb R^a,\lambda_a)$ and $H_b=L^2(\mathbb R^b,\lambda_b)$, with $L^2$ understood as the almost-everywhere quotient of square-integrable measurable functions ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]). Then there is a unique linear isometry

$$\Theta:H_a\widehat\otimes H_b\longrightarrow L^2(\mathbb R^{a+b})$$

with $\Theta(f\otimes g)(x,y)=f(x)g(y)$ for all $f\in H_a$, $g\in H_b$ and a.e. $(x,y)$, and $\Theta$ is onto: it is a surjective linear isometry, hence unitary. Vector-valued or spin factors follow by finite component sums. No identification of non-Euclidean product measures is asserted.
items.strategy: Check the inner-product identity on finite sums by Fubini for the L¹ products ff' and gg', extend isometrically, and prove density of the product span by a box-integral argument: sections with vanishing box integrals vanish a.e. by finite-measure uniqueness on the rational-box pi-system.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, §1.4 pp. 45-47 (tensor products of L² spaces)
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products', §1

items.title: Nuclear bounded cyclicity for trace-class operators
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and for $u,v\in H$ let $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]).

(a) For every bounded $B\in\mathcal B(H)$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]),

$$BT_{u,v}=T_{Bu,v},\qquad T_{u,v}B=T_{u,B^*v},$$

with the Hilbert adjoint $B^*$ ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]).

(b) Let $T\in\mathcal B(H)$ be trace class and let $T=\sum_jT_{u_j,v_j}$ be a nuclear representation, i.e. the partial sums converge to $T$ in operator norm and $\sum_j\|u_j\|\,\|v_j\|<\infty$ ([[lem-nuclear-series-characterizes-trace-norm]], [[def-trace-class-operator]]). Then for every bounded $B$

$$\operatorname{tr}(BT)=\sum_j\langle Bu_j,v_j\rangle,\qquad \operatorname{tr}(TB)=\sum_j\langle u_j,B^*v_j\rangle,$$

both series converging absolutely with $\bigl|\operatorname{tr}(BT)\bigr|\le\|B\|\sum_j\|u_j\|\,\|v_j\|$, and $\operatorname{tr}(BT)=\operatorname{tr}(TB)$ ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]). In particular $\operatorname{tr}(BT)=\operatorname{tr}(TB)$ for every trace-class $T$ and bounded $B$, and $\operatorname{tr}(T_{u,v})=\langle u,v\rangle$. No cyclic permutation of unbounded operators is asserted.
items.strategy: Compute the rank-one identities and |tr(T_{v,u})|≤‖v‖‖u‖ first, pass to nuclear series by absolute convergence and the trace-class ideal estimates, and then to bounded multipliers with the bound ‖B‖Σ‖v_j‖‖u_j‖; the Lipschitz clause follows from the rank-one norm and nuclear estimates.

references.title: G. Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017), §3.6 pp. 93-96 (trace class, nuclear series and cyclicity)
A. W. Knapp, Advanced Real Analysis, Chapter II §5 (trace-class operators and their ideal properties)

items.title: Complex Gaussian continuation
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). For $z\in\mathbb C$ with $\operatorname{Re}z>0$ and $n\ge1$ let

$$G_n(z):=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e^{-z|x|^2}\,dx,$$

where $dx$ is product Lebesgue measure and the complex integral is computed from its real and imaginary parts. Equivalently, the absolutely convergent improper multiple integral used here is the cube-truncation limit $\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{[-R,R]^n}e^{-z|x|^2}\,dx$ of these finite Lebesgue integrals. For $n=1$ it also equals the sum of the two separately convergent one-sided improper Riemann integrals at $0$, computed componentwise ([[def-improper-integral-at-infinity]]); this agreement is proved below. Then:

(a) $G_n(z)$ converges absolutely for every $z$ with $\operatorname{Re}z>0$, and $G_1$ is holomorphic on the right half-plane $\Omega:=\{z\in\mathbb C:\operatorname{Re}z>0\}$ with $G_1'(z)=-\int_{\mathbb R}x^2e^{-zx^2}dx$ ([[def-complex-differentiability-holomorphic-and-entire]], [[def-complex-domain]]);

(b) with $\operatorname{Log}$ the principal logarithm and the branch $z^{-1/2}:=\exp\bigl(-\tfrac12\operatorname{Log}z\bigr)$ on the slit plane ([[def-complex-logarithms-principal-logarithm-and-complex-powers]], [[cor-principal-logarithm-is-holomorphic-on-the-slit-plane]]),

$$G_1(z)=\sqrt{\pi}\,z^{-1/2},\qquad G_1(z)^2=\frac{\pi}{z}\qquad(z\in\Omega),$$

the value on the positive real axis being $G_1(t)=\sqrt{\pi/t}$ for $t>0$;

(c) for every $n\ge1$ and $z\in\Omega$, $G_n(z)=G_1(z)^n=(\pi/z)^{n/2}$, the power being the branch $(\pi/z)^{n/2}=\exp\bigl(\tfrac n2(\log\pi-\operatorname{Log}z)\bigr)$.

In particular the factor $(1+i\tau)^{-1/2}$ is defined by this branch for every real $\tau$, since $\operatorname{Re}(1+i\tau)=1>0$. No asymptotic or distributional interpretation is asserted.
items.strategy: Reduce the positive-parameter identity to the published Gaussian transform at frequency zero, prove holomorphy of G by dominated convergence of the difference quotients, identify the branch on (0,∞) and extend by the identity theorem on the half-plane domain, then factor the d-dimensional integral by Tonelli.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, §7.2-7.3 pp. 167-172 (Gaussian kernels for the free evolution)
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 1 'Wave Mechanics' (Gaussian integrals and free packets)

items.title: Momentum Fourier Jacobian: the unitary momentum representation
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), let $d\ge1$ and $\hbar>0$. Write $\mathcal F_2$ for the unitary Plancherel transform extending $\widehat f(\xi)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ ([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]); the $L^2$ spaces are Hilbert spaces by [[thm-riesz-fischer-completeness-of-l-p]] and [[def-hilbert-space]]. For $\psi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$, denote by $\widehat\psi$ the continuous representative of $\mathcal F_2\psi$ given by that absolutely convergent integral.

(a) For $\psi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$ the momentum wavefunction

$$\psi_p(p):=(2\pi\hbar)^{-d/2}\int_{\mathbb R^d}e^{-ip\cdot x/\hbar}\psi(x)\,dx$$

is well defined, bounded and continuous, and $\psi_p(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-d/2}\widehat\psi\bigl(p/(2\pi\hbar)\bigr)$ for every $p$; here $\widehat\psi$ is the stated continuous representative, not a point evaluation of an $L^2$ equivalence class.

(b) The dilation operator $D_\hbar g(p):=(2\pi\hbar)^{-d/2}g\bigl(p/(2\pi\hbar)\bigr)$ is a surjective linear isometry of $L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ onto itself, with inverse $D_\hbar^{-1}g(\xi)=(2\pi\hbar)^{d/2}g(2\pi\hbar\,\xi)$.

(c) The formula $U_0\psi:=\psi_p$ defines a linear isometry $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)\to L^2(\mathbb R^d)$ (for the Lebesgue spaces $dx$ and $dp$) that extends uniquely to a surjective linear isometry $U:L^2(\mathbb R^d,dx)\to L^2(\mathbb R^d,dp)$; on Schwartz functions $U=D_\hbar\mathcal F_2$, and for every $\psi\in L^2(\mathbb R^d)$,

$$\|U\psi\|_{L^2(dp)}=\|\psi\|_{L^2(dx)} .$$

The normalization statement is: the substitution $\xi=p/(2\pi\hbar)$ carries $d\xi=(2\pi\hbar)^{-d}dp$, and the factor $(2\pi\hbar)^{-d/2}$ in $U_0$ is exactly what makes $U$ an isometry with respect to $dp$. No physical identification of $U\psi$ with a measured momentum distribution is made.
items.strategy: Rewrite the momentum integral as the L¹ Fourier transform at ξ=p/(2πℏ), use the dilation/change-of-variable law |det A| of the Fourier transform for the normalization factor, conclude isometry on Schwartz functions, and extend by the bounded-extension theorem.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, §7.1 pp. 161-165 (Fourier conventions and momentum domains)
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, §2.4 pp. 28-32 (momentum-space wavefunction)

items.title: Separable partial trace and its basic properties
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be nonzero complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let $H\widehat\otimes K$ be their completed tensor product ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]); write $T_{x,z}x'=\langle x',z\rangle x$ for rank-one operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]) and $\operatorname{tr}$ for the trace of a trace-class operator ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]).

(a) There is a unique linear map $\operatorname{Tr}_K:\mathcal S_1(H\widehat\otimes K)\to\mathcal S_1(H)$ with

$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl((\operatorname{Tr}_KT)A\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(T(A\otimes I_K)\bigr)$$

for every trace-class $T$ and every $A\in\mathcal B(H)$; it satisfies $\|\operatorname{Tr}_KT\|_1\le\|T\|_1$ and is independent of any chosen orthonormal basis of $K$.

(b) $\operatorname{Tr}_K$ maps self-adjoint positive trace-class operators to self-adjoint positive trace-class operators (positivity in the bounded-operator sense of [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]), is trace preserving ($\operatorname{tr}\operatorname{Tr}_KT=\operatorname{tr}T$), and maps density operators to density operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]).

(c) On rank-one operators, $\operatorname{Tr}_KT_{u\otimes v,u'\otimes v'}=\langle v,v'\rangle_K\,T_{u,u'}$.

The analogous map $\operatorname{Tr}_H$ satisfies $\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{Tr}_HT)A)=\operatorname{tr}(T(I_H\otimes A))$ for $A\in\mathcal B(K)$. No claim is made about instruments or conditioning.
items.strategy: Define Tr_K on rank-one maps by the basis formula, prove trace-norm convergence of the resulting series (nuclear representation), establish the trace-pairing identity for rank-one maps and extend by absolute convergence, deduce uniqueness from testing against rank-one A, and get positivity by testing against x∈H.

references.title: G. Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017), §3.6 pp. 93-96 (trace-class operators and partial traces)
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products', §3 pp. 9-12

items.title: Finite-ancilla complete positivity of countable Kraus maps
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $(M_a)_{a\ge1}$ be bounded operators on $H$ with $\sum_{a\le N}M_a^*M_a\to I$ strongly, and let $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_aM_a\rho M_a^*$ be the map of [[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]]. Here a map on trace-class operators is **completely positive on finite-dimensional ancillas** when, for every finite-dimensional complex inner product space $C$, its matrixwise amplification $I_C\otimes\Phi$ preserves self-adjoint positive trace-class operators on $C\widehat\otimes H$. Then for every finite-dimensional complex inner product space $C$ the amplification

$$I_C\otimes\Phi:S_1(C\widehat\otimes H)\to S_1(C\widehat\otimes H)$$

is well defined by the trace-norm convergent series $\sum_a(I_C\otimes M_a)R(I_C\otimes M_a^*)$ and preserves positivity: every self-adjoint positive trace-class $R$ (positivity in the sense of [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]) has $I_C\otimes\Phi(R)$ self-adjoint positive. Hence $\Phi$ is completely positive on every finite-dimensional ancilla in the stated sense.
items.strategy: On the dense span of elementary tensors the amplification of each summand is a positive map and the sum converges in trace norm by the nuclear estimates; positivity passes to the trace-norm limit, and the finite-dimensional statements reduce to finite sums.

references.title: G. Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017), §3.6 pp. 93-96 (trace-class amplification)
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products' (composite systems and amplification)

items.title: Local trace-preserving Kraus maps do not change the opposite reduced state
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be complex Hilbert spaces, let $(M_a)_{a\ge1}$ be bounded operators on $K$ with $\sum_{a\le N}M_a^*M_a\to I_K$ strongly, and let $R$ be a trace-class operator on $H\widehat\otimes K$. In this statement, $R\ge0$ means that $R$ is self-adjoint and $\langle Rx,x\rangle\ge0$ for every $x$, as in [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]. Then the series (when either factor is $\{0\}$, use the zero partial-trace maps $\operatorname{Tr}_K:\mathcal S_1(\{0\})\to\mathcal S_1(H)$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_H:\mathcal S_1(\{0\})\to\mathcal S_1(K)$; when both factors are nonzero, use the partial traces of [[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]])

$$\sum_{a\ge1}(I_H\otimes M_a)R(I_H\otimes M_a^*)$$

converges in trace norm, its sum $\Phi(R)$ is trace class with $\operatorname{tr}\Phi(R)=\operatorname{tr}R$ and $\Phi(R)\ge0$ if $R\ge0$, and the reduced state on $H$ is unchanged:

$$\operatorname{Tr}_K\Phi(R)=\operatorname{Tr}_KR .$$

By symmetry, a local map $R\mapsto\sum_a(N_a\otimes I_K)R(N_a^*\otimes I_K)$ on the first factor also leaves $\operatorname{Tr}_HR$ fixed. Selective conditioning (one summand normalized by its nonzero trace) is not covered.
items.strategy: Test the identity against an arbitrary bounded A on H, use the defining property of the partial trace to move A⊗I, cyclicity for bounded operators and the completeness identity Σ_a M_a*M_a=I, and density of the relevant operators.

references.title: MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products', §3 pp. 9-12
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, §6.3 pp. 121-128 (local operations and reduced states)

items.title: Infinite Schmidt decomposition and the pure product criterion
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and let $H,K$ be nonzero complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]) with $H\widehat\otimes K$ their completed tensor product ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). A **product vector** means an elementary tensor $v\otimes u$ with $v\in H$ and $u\in K$. Then for every $\Psi\in H\widehat\otimes K$ there are an at most countable index set $J$, orthonormal families $(v_r)_{r\in J}\subseteq H$ and $(u_r)_{r\in J}\subseteq K$, and numbers $s_r>0$ with

$$\Psi=\sum_{r\in J}s_r\,v_r\otimes u_r\qquad\text{(norm convergence in }H\widehat\otimes K),$$

and $\|\Psi\|^2=\sum_rs_r^2$. The $s_r$ are the positive square roots of the nonzero eigenvalues of $CC^*$, where $C:\overline{K_0}\to H_0$ is the linear coefficient operator on countable closed factor supports of $\Psi$, defined below; if $J$ is infinite then $s_r\to0$. For $\|\Psi\|=1$ the reduced density $\rho=\operatorname{Tr}_KT_{\Psi,\Psi}$ has $\operatorname{tr}\rho^2=\sum_rs_r^4$, and $\operatorname{tr}\rho^2=1$ holds exactly when exactly one $s_r$ is nonzero, i.e. exactly when $\Psi$ is a product vector. No assertion about separability of mixed density operators is made here.

For clarity, choose finite algebraic tensors converging to $\Psi$ and let $H_0\subseteq H$, $K_0\subseteq K$ be the closed spans of their factor vectors. These supports have finite/countable orthonormal bases, and $\Psi\in H_0\widehat\otimes K_0$. The conjugate Hilbert space $\overline{K_0}$ consists of symbols $\bar z$, with $a\bar z:=\overline{\bar a z}$ and $\langle\bar z,\bar w\rangle_{\overline{K_0}}:=\langle w,z\rangle_{K_0}$. For an orthonormal basis $(f_j)$ of $K_0$, write $\Psi=\sum_jh_j\otimes f_j$ and set $C\bar f_j=h_j$, extending linearly and continuously. The positive singular values and the nonzero spectrum of $CC^*$ are independent of these supports and bases, as the reduced-state identity proved below shows.
items.strategy: Expand Ψ against an orthonormal basis of K to obtain coefficient vectors h_j, build the compact coefficient operator C:ℓ²→H and diagonalize the positive compact operator CC*; define the partners v_r with the coefficient identities and verify orthonormality, completeness and norm convergence, then read the reduced eigenvalues off the partial trace.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, §1.4 pp. 45-47 and Ch. 3 (compact operators and spectral decomposition)
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products', §§1-3

items.title: Abstract trace-class instruments: effects and Heisenberg duality
items.strategy: Use the trace-class pairing functional T↦tr J_B(T), evaluate it on rank-one maps, obtain a bounded sesquilinear form, apply Riesz representation to get F_B with 0≤F_B≤I, and transfer the identities by linearity and trace-norm continuity.

MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 4 'Dirac's Bra and Ket Notation' (effects and measurement formulation)

items.title: Finite Naimark compression: a finite POVM as a compression of a PVM
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and $(F_1,\dots,F_n)$ a finite POVM on $H$: a finite family of bounded self-adjoint operators $0\le F_a\le I$ with $\sum_aF_a=I$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]]). Let $C=\mathbb C^n$ with standard orthonormal basis $(e_a)$ and form $H\widehat\otimes C$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). Then

$$W:H\to H\widehat\otimes C,\qquad W\psi:=\sum_{a=1}^nF_a^{1/2}\psi\otimes e_a,$$

is a linear isometry, the operators $P_a:=I_H\otimes T_{e_a,e_a}$ are orthogonal projections with $\sum_aP_a=I$ (a finite PVM on $\{1,\dots,n\}$, [[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]), and

$$W^*P_aW=F_a\qquad(a=1,\dots,n).$$

The square roots $F_a^{1/2}$ are the positive square roots supplied by the bounded functional calculus. The construction asserts no physical realization of the ancilla.
items.strategy: Take bounded positive square roots by the continuous functional calculus, compute ‖Wψ‖²=Σ_a⟨F_aψ,ψ⟩=‖ψ‖², and identify the compressions W*P_aW by matrix elements in the ancilla basis.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Ch. 3 pp. 90-100 (bounded self-adjoint calculus)
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 4 'Dirac's Bra and Ket Notation'

items.title: Countable Kraus isometric dilation and partial-trace recovery
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let $(M_{a,r})_{a,r\ge1}$ be bounded operators on $H$ with

$$\sum_{a\le A,\,r\le R}M_{a,r}^*M_{a,r}\longrightarrow I\qquad\text{strongly as }A,R\to\infty .$$

Let $(e_{a,r})_{a,r\ge1}$ be the standard orthonormal basis of $\ell^2$ and form $H\widehat\otimes\ell^2$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). Then

$$W:H\to H\widehat\otimes\ell^2,\qquad W\psi:=\sum_{a,r\ge1}M_{a,r}\psi\otimes e_{a,r}$$

is a linear isometry; for each outcome label $a$ the strong limit $P_a:=\sum_{r\ge1}I_H\otimes T_{e_{a,r},e_{a,r}}$ is an orthogonal projection ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]), the family $(P_a)_{a\ge1}$ consists of pairwise orthogonal projections with $\sum_aP_a=I$ strongly, and

$$W^*P_aW=\sum_{r\ge1}M_{a,r}^*M_{a,r}=:F_a ;$$

moreover the partial trace of the dilated state over $\ell^2$ recovers the Kraus instrument: for every trace-class $\rho$ on $H$,

$$\operatorname{Tr}_{\ell^2}\bigl(W\rho W^*\bigr)=\sum_{a,r\ge1}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^* ,$$

the series converging in trace norm and the right side being the map of [[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]]. This realizes the specified family; it is not a classification of all channels.
items.strategy: Compute ‖Wψ‖² by orthonormality of the ancilla basis and strong completeness, identify the compression of each P_a by its matrix elements, and use the partial-trace defining identity to recover the Kraus instrument.

references.title: G. Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017), §3.6 pp. 93-96 (trace-class dilation computations)
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products' (ancilla constructions)

items.title: Continuous measurable Kraus instruments: isometry, POVM and trace-norm integration
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a $\sigma$-finite measure space, $H$ a nonzero separable complex Hilbert space, and $(M_r)_{r\ge1}$ bounded operator-valued maps on $X$ such that:

(i) for every $\psi\in H$ the map $x\mapsto M_r(x)\psi$ is strongly measurable for each $r$ ([[def-strongly-measurable-banach-valued-function]]) and

$$\int_X\sum_{r\ge1}\|M_r(x)\psi\|^2\,d\mu(x)=\|\psi\|^2\qquad(\psi\in H).$$

Here $E:=\ell^2(H)$ is the space of sequences $z=(z_r)_{r\ge1}$ with $\sum_r\|z_r\|^2<\infty$, with inner product $\langle z,w\rangle_E:=\sum_r\langle z_r,w_r\rangle_H$. Define $L^2(X,\mu;E)$ as the vector space of strongly measurable fields $f:X\to E$ with $\int_X\|f(x)\|_E^2d\mu<\infty$, modulo equality almost everywhere; its inner product is $\langle[f],[g]\rangle:=\int_X\langle f(x),g(x)\rangle_Ed\mu$. The proof establishes that both spaces are Hilbert spaces before using adjoints or PVMs on this target.

Then:

(a) the formula $W\psi(x):=(M_r(x)\psi)_r$ defines a linear isometry $W:H\to L^2(X,\mu;\ell^2(H))$;

(b) for $B\in\Sigma$ the multiplication operator $P(B)$ by $\mathbf 1_B$ is a projection-valued measure on $(X,\Sigma)$, and $F(B):=W^*P(B)W$ is a normalized POVM. Here a POVM is a weakly countably additive map $F:\Sigma\to\mathcal B(H)$ whose values are self-adjoint positive contractions, with $F(\varnothing)=0$ and $F(X)=I$; positivity is in the sense of [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]];

(c) for every self-adjoint positive trace-class $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ ([[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]], [[def-trace-class-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]) the Bochner integral

$$I_B(\rho):=\sum_{n\ge1}w_n\int_B\sum_{r\ge1}T_{M_r(x)u_n,M_r(x)u_n}\,d\mu(x)$$

converges in trace norm and defines a positive trace-class operator with $\operatorname{tr}I_B(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F(B))$; the map $B\mapsto I_B(\rho)$ is countably additive in trace norm and $I_X$ is trace preserving, so $I$ is an abstract instrument in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]]; moreover $\operatorname{tr}(I_B(\rho)A)=\sum_r\int_B\operatorname{tr}(M_r(x)\rho M_r(x)^*A)\,d\mu(x)$ for bounded $A$, and finite-dimensional ancilla amplifications preserve positivity;

(d) the conditional update at an event $B$ with $p(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F(B))>0$ is $I_B(\rho)/p(B)$. The normalization is integrated over events; no pointwise identity $\sum_rM_r(x)^*M_r(x)=I$ is assumed. Universal normal-instrument representation is not claimed.
items.strategy: Prove the isometry from the normalization hypothesis, define the PVM and POVM by compression, construct I_B from rank-one contributions with Bochner measurability and Tonelli bounds, and establish well-definedness, positivity, additivity and trace preservation by testing against bounded A.

references.title: G. Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017), Ch. 1-3 (Bochner integration, trace-class Banach space and duality)
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 4 'Dirac's Bra and Ket Notation' (POVM formulation)

items.title: Marker overlap contraction of the two-path cross term
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(D,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a $\sigma$-finite measure space, let $L^2(D,\mu)$ denote the quotient of square-integrable measurable functions modulo almost-everywhere equality ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]), let $K$ be a complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) with unit vectors $e_1,e_2$, let $a,b\in L^2(D,\mu)$ be unit vectors, and let $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb C$ with $|\alpha|^2+|\beta|^2=1$. Choose measurable representatives of $a,b$; all displayed pointwise expressions are understood almost everywhere, and the integrals below are independent of the representatives. Put

$$\Psi:=\alpha\,a\otimes e_1+\beta\,b\otimes e_2\in L^2(D)\widehat\otimes K .$$

Then:

(a) the reduced positive trace-class weight $\rho:=\operatorname{Tr}_KT_{\Psi,\Psi}$ on $L^2(D)$ is

$$\rho=|\alpha|^2T_{a,a}+|\beta|^2T_{b,b}+\alpha\overline\beta\,\langle e_1,e_2\rangle\,T_{a,b}+\overline\alpha\beta\,\langle e_2,e_1\rangle\,T_{b,a};$$

(b) for every measurable $B\subseteq D$ with finite measure, writing $P_B$ for the multiplication operator by $\mathbf 1_B$,

$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_B)=\int_B\Bigl(|\alpha|^2|a|^2+|\beta|^2|b|^2+2\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\alpha\overline\beta\langle e_1,e_2\rangle\,a(x)\overline{b(x)}\bigr)\Bigr)d\mu ;$$

(c) the marker overlap contracts the cross term: $|\langle e_1,e_2\rangle|\le1$, and if $e_1\perp e_2$ the cross term in (b) vanishes, leaving the incoherent weight $|\alpha|^2|a|^2+|\beta|^2|b|^2$.

The weight satisfies $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\|\Psi\|^2=1+2\operatorname{Re}(\alpha\overline\beta\langle a,b\rangle\langle e_1,e_2\rangle)$; it is a density operator precisely when $\|\Psi\|=1$. The stated assumptions do not force this normalization. These are identities for the specified vector and its unnormalized weight; they assert no measured detector law and cover no selective conditioning.
items.strategy: Write the rank-one reduced state via the partial-trace pairing identity against T_{f,g}, expand the four products, and read off the bin weights as the diagonal pairing of ρ with the multiplication indicator.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, §6.3 pp. 121-128 (reduced states and marker-induced loss of coherence)
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products', §3

items.title: Exact free Gaussian propagation
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix $m>0$, $\hbar>0$, $\sigma>0$ and real $x_0,p_0$, and let

$$\psi_0(x):=(2\pi\sigma^2)^{-1/4}\exp\Bigl(-\frac{(x-x_0)^2}{4\sigma^2}\Bigr)\exp\Bigl(i\frac{p_0(x-x_0)}{\hbar}\Bigr),\qquad x\in\mathbb R .$$

Let $H_0$ be the free operator of clause (b) of [[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]] with $c:=2\pi^2\hbar^2/m$ and $b:=0$, i.e.

$$H_0:=\mathcal F_2^*\,M_{2\pi^2\hbar^2\xi^2/m}\,\mathcal F_2,\qquad D(H_0)=\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R):\xi^2\mathcal F_2f\in L^2(\mathbb R)\},$$

which is self-adjoint with $D(H_0)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$ and $H_0f=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Delta f$ for $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R)$. Let $U$ be the momentum transform of [[lem-nrqm-composites-momentum-fourier-jacobian]], the surjective isometry $L^2(\mathbb R,dx)\to L^2(\mathbb R,dp)$ with $U=D_\hbar\circ\mathcal F_2$ on $\mathcal S(\mathbb R)$. For $t\in\mathbb R$ put $\tau:=\frac{\hbar t}{2m\sigma^2}$ and

$$\psi_t(x):=(2\pi\sigma^2)^{-1/4}(1+i\tau)^{-1/2}\exp\Bigl(-\frac{(x-x_0-p_0t/m)^2}{4\sigma^2(1+i\tau)}+i\frac{p_0(x-x_0)}{\hbar}-i\frac{p_0^2t}{2m\hbar}\Bigr),$$

where $z^{-1/2}:=\exp\bigl(-\tfrac12\operatorname{Log}z\bigr)$ is the principal branch of [[def-complex-logarithms-principal-logarithm-and-complex-powers]], legitimate at $z=1+i\tau$ because $\operatorname{Re}(1+i\tau)=1>0$. Let $Qf(x)=xf(x)$ and $Pf(x)=-i\hbar f'(x)$ act on $\mathcal S(\mathbb R)$. Then:

(a) $\psi_0\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R)$, $\|\psi_0\|_2=1$, and for every $t$ one has $\psi_t\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R)\subseteq D(H_0)$; the map $t\mapsto\psi_t$ is continuously differentiable $\mathbb R\to L^2(\mathbb R)$ with $\psi_t\in D(H_0)$ and $\frac{d}{dt}\psi_t=-\frac{i}{\hbar}H_0\psi_t$, and consequently $\psi_t=e^{-itH_0/\hbar}\psi_0$, where $e^{-itH_0/\hbar}:=e^{itT}$ with $T:=-H_0/\hbar$ denotes the unitary group generated by the self-adjoint operator $T$ ([[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]]).

(b) _Position density._ $|\psi_t(x)|^2=\bigl(2\pi\sigma^2(1+\tau^2)\bigr)^{-1/2}\exp\bigl(-(x-x_0-p_0t/m)^2/(2\sigma^2(1+\tau^2))\bigr)$; it is a probability density of mean $x_0+p_0t/m$ and variance $\sigma^2(1+\tau^2)$.

(c) _Momentum density._ $|U\psi_t(p)|^2=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,(\sigma/\hbar)\exp\bigl(-2\sigma^2(p-p_0)^2/\hbar^2\bigr)=|U\psi_0(p)|^2$ for almost every $p$; it is a probability density of mean $p_0$ and variance $\hbar^2/(4\sigma^2)$, independent of $t$.

(d) _Standard deviations._ With $\Delta Q:=\|(Q-\langle Q\psi_t,\psi_t\rangle)\psi_t\|_2$ and $\Delta P:=\|(P-\langle P\psi_t,\psi_t\rangle)\psi_t\|_2$ one has $\Delta Q=\sigma\sqrt{1+\tau^2}$, $\Delta P=\hbar/(2\sigma)$ and

$$\Delta Q\,\Delta P=\frac{\hbar}{2}\sqrt{1+\tau^2}\ \ge\ \frac{\hbar}{2},$$

with equality exactly at $t=0$; the lower bound $\hbar/2$ is the one supplied by clause (d) of [[lem-nrqm-composites-weak-form-robertson-uncertainty]] with $c=\hbar$.

(e) _Scope._ These are exact conditional calculations for the free model defined by $H_0$; no measurement, instrument or laboratory preparation is described, and nothing here asserts that a physical wave packet is Gaussian.
items.strategy: Transform the initial Gaussian explicitly, multiply the momentum wavefunction by e^{−itp²/(2mℏ)}, complete the square with a parameter of positive real part so the continued Gaussian identity applies, and read the moments off the resulting Gaussian densities; the uncertainty clause uses the Robertson bound with the exact variances.

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Thm 7.8 p. 168 and §7.3 (free evolution)

items.title: Joint PVM construction for strongly commuting regular projection-valued measures
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let $E,F$ be **regular** projection-valued measures on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]) satisfying the strong commutation relation

$$E(B)F(C)=F(C)E(B)\qquad\text{for all Borel }B,C\subseteq\mathbb R .$$

Then there is a unique regular projection-valued measure $G$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R^2$ with

$$G(B\times C)=E(B)F(C)\qquad\text{for every Borel rectangle }B\times C,$$

where rectangle means a measurable rectangle in the sense of [[def-measurable-rectangle]]. Its marginals are $G(B\times\mathbb R)=E(B)$ and $G(\mathbb R\times C)=F(C)$.

For the scalar construction, let $\mathcal A_0$ be the algebra of finite unions of Borel rectangles, and define $P_0(\bigsqcup_{i=1}^n B_i\times C_i):=\sum_{i=1}^nE(B_i)F(C_i)$ on disjoint rectangular decompositions. For every $\psi\in H$, $\mu_\psi(A):=\langle P_0(A)\psi,\psi\rangle$ is a finite premeasure on $\mathcal A_0$ and has a unique extension $G_\psi=\langle G(\cdot)\psi,\psi\rangle$ to the Borel $\sigma$-algebra. For $x,y\in H$, define the polarized measure $\nu_{x,y}:=\frac14\sum_{k=0}^3 i^kG_{x+i^ky}$. Then every Borel $S\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ has a unique bounded operator $G(S)$ satisfying $\langle G(S)x,y\rangle=\nu_{x,y}(S)$ for all $x,y\in H$, and $0\le G(S)\le I$.
items.strategy: Build the finitely additive projection P on the algebra of finite disjoint rectangle unions, prove the scalar set functions are premeasures by compact inner approximation, extend by Carathéodory, polarize, represent each bounded sesquilinear form by Riesz to obtain G(S) with 0≤G(S)≤I, and verify the product identities by uniqueness on rectangles.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Thm 3.1-3.2 pp. 90-92 (projection-valued measures and Borel calculus)
A. W. Knapp, Advanced Real Analysis, Ch. II-III (Carathéodory extension, measure uniqueness and regularity)

items.title: Compatible Lüders repeatability
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space, let $E,F$ be regular projection-valued measures on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ with $E(B)F(C)=F(C)E(B)$ for all Borel $B,C\subseteq\mathbb R$, and let $G$ be the joint projection-valued measure on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R^2$ with $G(B\times C)=E(B)F(C)$ and marginals $E,F$ ([[thm-nrqm-composites-joint-pvm-construction]]). Fix finite families of Borel sets $B_1,\dots,B_n$ with $B_i\cap B_k=\varnothing$ for $i\ne k$ and $C_1,\dots,C_m$ with $C_j\cap C_l=\varnothing$ for $j\ne l$, put

$$P_i:=E(B_i),\qquad Q_j:=F(C_j),\qquad R_{ij}:=P_iQ_j ,$$

and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $H$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]](a)). The listed projections are stipulated to be outcomes of ideal Lüders instruments, with outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_i)$ and post-measurement states $\rho_i:=P_i\rho P_i/\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_i)$ when $\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_i)>0$, and likewise for $(Q_j)$. If either listed family fails to sum to the identity, include its complementary projection $I-\sum_iP_i$ or $I-\sum_jQ_j$ as an additional outcome; only probabilities for the listed outcomes are displayed below. A sequential run measures the first instrument and then the second on the resulting state. Then:

(a) $P_i,Q_j$ and $R_{ij}$ are orthogonal projections ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]), $R_{ij}=Q_jP_i=G(B_i\times C_j)$, and $P_iP_k=0$ for $i\ne k$, $Q_jQ_l=0$ for $j\ne l$, $R_{ij}R_{kl}=0$ whenever $(i,j)\ne(k,l)$.

(b) The probability of the listed ordered outcome pair $(i\ \text{then}\ j)$ equals, when $\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_i)>0$, $\operatorname{tr}(P_i\rho P_iQ_j)/\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_i)\cdot\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_i)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho R_{ij})$, and is zero if the first outcome has zero probability; the same number is obtained in the reversed order, so the sequential order of the two compatible sharp measurements gives the same masses to all listed outcome pairs:
$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl(P_i\rho P_iQ_j\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(Q_j\rho Q_jP_i\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho R_{ij})=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,G(B_i\times C_j)\bigr).$$

(c) If $\operatorname{tr}(\rho R_{ij})>0$, the conditional state after the pair is order-independent:
$$\frac{Q_jP_i\rho P_iQ_j}{\operatorname{tr}(\rho R_{ij})}=\frac{P_iQ_j\rho Q_jP_i}{\operatorname{tr}(\rho R_{ij})}=\frac{R_{ij}\,\rho\,R_{ij}}{\operatorname{tr}(\rho R_{ij})},$$
and it is a density operator.

(d) *Repeatability.* Under the positive-probability hypothesis $\operatorname{tr}(\rho R_{ij})>0$ of (c), with $\sigma:=R_{ij}\rho R_{ij}/\operatorname{tr}(\rho R_{ij})$ one has $\operatorname{tr}(\sigma R_{ij})=1$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\sigma P_i)=\operatorname{tr}(\sigma Q_j)=1$, and the Lüders update by $R_{ij}$, $P_i$ or $Q_j$ leaves $\sigma$ unchanged: $R_{ij}\sigma R_{ij}/\operatorname{tr}(\sigma R_{ij})=P_i\sigma P_i/\operatorname{tr}(\sigma P_i)=Q_j\sigma Q_j/\operatorname{tr}(\sigma Q_j)=\sigma$. Thus immediate repetition of the compatible pair, or of either single sharp measurement, reproduces the same outcomes with certainty.

(e) If $\bigcup_jC_j=\mathbb R$ then $\sum_j\operatorname{tr}(\rho R_{ij})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_i)$, and if $\bigcup_iB_i=\mathbb R$ then $\sum_i\operatorname{tr}(\rho R_{ij})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho Q_j)$: the joint law has the sharp-bin marginals.

(f) *Scope.* All of this is a conditional calculation for the stipulated ideal Lüders instrument and the joint PVM $G$; no claim is made that a laboratory apparatus realizes the Lüders instrument or the joint measurement, and no dynamical time development is described.
items.strategy: Use Trace cyclicity with the bounded projections and the joint spectral identity G(B_i×C_j)=P_iQ_j for probability and update, and idempotence P_iQ_jP_iQ_j=P_iQ_j for repeatability; order independence follows from commutativity.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, §1.4 p. 15 (ideal measurement) and §6.1.1 pp. 108-109
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 4 'Dirac's Bra and Ket Notation' (projective measurements)

items.title: Bell reduced state
items.statement:
Let $V=W=\mathbb C^2$ with the standard inner product and orthonormal basis $e_+=\binom{1}{0}$, $e_-=\binom{0}{1}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), and let

$$\Psi:=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\bigl(e_+\otimes e_--e_-\otimes e_+\bigr)\in V\otimes W .$$

Here a **product vector** means an elementary tensor $v\otimes u$ with $v\in V$ and $u\in W$; $T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ is the rank-one density operator determined by the unit vector $\Psi$.

Then:

(a) $\|\Psi\|=1$, and the coefficient matrix of $\Psi$ in the bases $(e_+,e_-)$ is $C=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}$;

(b) the partial traces satisfy $\operatorname{Tr}_WT_{\Psi,\Psi}=CC^*=\tfrac12 I_V$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_VT_{\Psi,\Psi}=C^*C=\tfrac12 I_W$, so both reduced states are the maximally mixed matrix $\tfrac12 I$;

(c) the reduced density $\rho=\tfrac12 I$ has eigenvalues $\tfrac12,\tfrac12$ and trace-square $\operatorname{tr}\rho^2=\tfrac12$, while $\operatorname{tr}(T_{\Psi,\Psi}^2)=1$; the Schmidt coefficients of $\Psi$ are $s_1=s_2=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$, and $\Psi$ is not a product vector.
items.strategy: Compute the matrix of Ψ in the standard product basis, apply the partial-trace formula by summing the relevant index pairs, and read eigenvalues and purity directly.

references.title: MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products', §§1-3
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, §6.1 pp. 105-115

items.title: Nonunique mixed ensemble
items.statement:
On $H=\mathbb C^2$ with the standard inner product and orthonormal basis $e_1=\binom10$, $e_2=\binom01$, put $e_\pm:=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}(e_1\pm e_2)$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]). Then the maximally mixed density operator $\frac12 I$ admits the two orthonormal convex decompositions

$$\frac12 I=\frac12T_{e_1,e_1}+\frac12T_{e_2,e_2}=\frac12T_{e_+,e_+}+\frac12T_{e_-,e_-},$$

where $(e_1,e_2)$ and $(e_+,e_-)$ are distinct orthonormal bases of $H$. Thus the same density operator has two distinct orthonormal convex decompositions into rank-one density operators.
items.strategy: Compute both convex combinations with the rank-one trace formula and the orthonormality of the two bases.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, §6.3 pp. 121-128 (density operators and their nonunique decompositions)
D. Skinner, Principles of Quantum Mechanics (Cambridge Part II, Michaelmas 2021), Chapter 10 'Interpreting Quantum Mechanics', pp. 1-12

items.title: Selective-conditioning counterexample
items.statement:
**False claim:** for every density operator $\rho$ on a tensor product $H\otimes K$ of finite-dimensional complex inner product spaces and every finite local family $(M_a)$ on $K$ with $\sum_aM_a^*M_a=I_K$, the conditional reduced state on $H$ after the outcome $a$ is again $\operatorname{Tr}_K\rho$ whenever its probability is positive.

The claim confuses the *nonselective* identity $\operatorname{Tr}_K\bigl(\sum_a(I\otimes M_a)\rho(I\otimes M_a^*)\bigr)=\operatorname{Tr}_K\rho$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-local-trace-preserving-no-signalling]] with the corresponding statement for one selected outcome. The displayed unit vector in $\mathbb C^2\otimes\mathbb C^2$ and one outcome of the explicitly defined projection instrument below refute the selective claim.
items.strategy: Compute the unnormalized conditional matrix from the partial-trace formula, normalize by its trace, compare with the unconditional maximally mixed reduced state, and verify the nonselective identity from the no-signalling lemma.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, §6.3 pp. 121-128
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 4 'Dirac's Bra and Ket Notation'
